messages:
mina: morning! quick kubectl/kubeconfig question on day 1. i merged my prod and ml-staging kubeconfigs and now `kubectl get pods -n feature-store` errors with Forbidden (user mina@redwood.com). should i be keeping them separate?
mina: exact: Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "mina@redwood.com" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "feature-store"
devops: welcome mina :) yes we prefer keeping prod config separate until your SSO groups are fully mapped. quick checks: `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=feature-store`. also `kubectl config view --minify` to confirm user.
mina: current-context -> ml-staging-mina
mina: auth can-i -> no
lucas: feature-store is owned by eng-mlops. we gate access via SSO group `eng-mlops-developers`. if you don't have that group mapped yet i'll create a short RoleBinding for onboarding.
mina: my SSO id is mina@redwood.com and github is minaw
lucas: i'll add a 4 hour RoleBinding with `view` in feature-store. creating with a dry-run then apply.
lucas: ran: kubectl create rolebinding rb-onboard-mina-feature -n feature-store --clusterrole=view --user=mina@redwood.com --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
lucas: applied. retry the get pods.
onboard-bot: Heads-up: onboarding doc "kube-access" has steps for persistent access and group mapping — https://internal.redwood/docs/onboard/kube-access. Temporary RBAC bindings expire automatically.
mina: works now, pods listed, thanks! :tada:
mina: follow-up: any safe aliases to avoid hitting prod accidentally? i'm on macOS.
devops: keep separate files like ~/.kube/prod and ~/.kube/ml-staging and set KUBECONFIG when you need to merge. i use a tiny helper: `kc() { KUBECONFIG="$HOME/.kube/$1" kubectl --context="$2" "${@:3}"; }` so `kc ml-staging ml-staging-mina get pods -n feature-store`. also add `kubectl config current-context` to your prompt.
mina: awesome, will add that. thanks everyone!
